core.title: Give every produced wagon artifact grammar-conformant contract and telemetry URNs
core.given: A wagon produces, or is being planned to produce, one or more artifacts, in whatever file or document they are defined.
core.when: The planner defines, modifies or reviews any wagon-produced artifact or its contract/telemetry URN.
core.then: Give each produced artifact a contract URN of the form contract:{theme}(:{category})*:{aspect}(.{variant})? and a telemetry URN of the form telemetry:{theme}(:{category})*:{aspect}(.{variant})?, following the artifact-naming grammar.
prefer: Write both URNs for every produced artifact, using the same theme/category/aspect path segments so the contract and telemetry identities line up.
Use ':' to separate theme, zero or more categories, and aspect; use a single '.' only before an optional variant on the last segment.
avoid: Producing an artifact with only a contract URN or only a telemetry URN.
URNs without the 'contract:' / 'telemetry:' scheme prefix, with no theme or aspect, or with '.' used as a category separator.
Inventing ad-hoc naming shapes that the artifact-naming file mapping cannot resolve.
core.why: Contract URNs map to contract files and telemetry URNs map to the telemetry location through the artifact-naming grammar; a URN outside that grammar breaks resolution for producers and consumers across wagon boundaries.
evidence: Every wagon-produced artifact, wherever it is defined, has both a contract URN and a telemetry URN.
Each contract URN matches contract:{theme}(:{category})*:{aspect}(.{variant})? and each telemetry URN matches telemetry:{theme}(:{category})*:{aspect}(.{variant})?.
verification: Scope: check all wagon-produced artifacts, existing and newly added, regardless of which file or document represents them; do not limit the check to changed produced-artifact declarations.

Validate each URN against the stated grammar: scheme prefix present, theme and aspect required, categories repeated zero or more times and separated by ':', variant optional and introduced by a single '.' on the final segment only.
A produced artifact carrying only one of the two URNs, or a URN outside the grammar, is a finding of this rule; the rule's term and finding ids are realization details and are not part of the core.

values: any file that defines or names a wagon-produced artifact (produced-artifact declaration, plan or acceptance artifact, contract or telemetry definition, implementation that declares produced artifacts or their URNs)
wagon-produced artifact defined, modified or renamed
contract/telemetry URN introduced or modified anywhere
wagon-produced artifact missing a contract or telemetry URN
URN not matching the contract/telemetry URN grammar

fires: The planner adds a new artifact to a wagon's produced outputs, in any representation.
The planner renames or restructures an existing produced artifact or its contract or telemetry URN.
The planner authors a new wagon that produces artifacts.
The planner reviews or audits an existing wagon whose produced artifacts may lack or misuse contract/telemetry URNs.
A plan, acceptance or implementation change defines a wagon-produced artifact or references/introduces its URN outside the wagon's produced-artifact declaration.
doesNotFire: Work that does not concern any wagon-produced artifact or its contract/telemetry URNs (e.g. prose-only edits to a wagon description, plan wording that names no produced artifact).
Artifacts a wagon only consumes, when no produced artifact or its URN is defined, changed or reviewed.

neutralityNotes: This rule is method-level rather than stack-mechanical: bun.json already names no stack, runtime, framework, language, package manager, file suffix or path, so the core keeps the artifact-naming URN grammar (contract:{theme}(:{category})*:{aspect}(.{variant})? and its telemetry twin) verbatim - the grammar is the obligation itself and is invariant across ATDD stacks. 'Wagon', 'artifact-naming grammar', 'contract files' and the telemetry location are method-level concepts (wagon also appears in the profile layout vocabulary), so they remain in the core. Bun-instance representation names were neutralized: 'wagon manifest' -> the wagon's produced-artifact declaration, 'WMBT'/'plan document' -> plan artifact. No profile data is needed: the rule is deliberately representation-agnostic and bun.json carries no paths, suffixes, tools or binding syntax, so profileRequirements is empty; in particular, the urn vocabulary group's artifact params cover identification URNs (component, acceptance, wmbt, wagon, ...) but not the contract/telemetry identity pair, and routing the grammar through new urn.contract/urn.telemetry keys was rejected because the grammar is the rule's obligation rather than stack-variable data (the owner may still choose to add such keys later). The per-fact 'note' texts of bun.json are dropped because the core activation fact schema carries only fact/values/observability.
